solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Very odd parts in Die Hard

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of the film title are the ones taken, first, third, fifth and seventh

explanation.surface: A remark that some roles in the action film Die Hard are very odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very' looks like it modifies 'odd', but it stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal intensifier synonym: 'dead easy' or 'dead right' uses the word to mean extremely.

clue.text: In Morecambe perhaps, politician — Independent — is a charlatan

indicators.note: the politician and the Independent sit in the middle of the comedian's first name

parts.note: Eric Morecambe was a famous British comedian, of Morecambe and Wise, so Morecambe is an example of an Eric
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An Independent politician in the seaside town of Morecambe is denounced as a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe reads as the Lancashire town, but it points to the comedian Eric Morecambe.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a quack doctor who relies on experience rather than learning, hence a fraud or impostor.

clue.text: Ranter, one interrupting winter piece by Debussy?

parts.note: DEC, December, is a winter month

indicators.note: the word for one breaks into the middle of the Debussy title

parts.note: La Mer is an orchestral work by Debussy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone loudly interrupts a performance of a wintry piece by Debussy.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who orates vehemently or speaks pompously, much like a person haranguing.

clue.text: British PM once receiving duke and soldiers making a racket

indicators.note: the former Prime Minister's name takes in the duke and soldiers, holding them inside

parts.note: Clement Attlee was British Prime Minister 1945-51
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A former British premier hosts a duke and some troops, and they make a lot of noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making a racket' suggests noise, but the racket is a bat used in an old shuttlecock game.
explanation.definitionFit: The bat used in the old game of shuttlecock, a forerunner of badminton, is a small racket.

clue.text: Brave fighters in endless pain, overwhelmed by swordsman: It's blooming fatal

indicators.note: the swordsman's word surrounds and swamps everything that comes before it in the clue

parts.note: a blade is a dashing swordsman

indicators.note: the fighters are placed within the shortened word for pain
the word for pain loses its final letter

parts.note: an ache is a pain
knights are brave armoured fighters

explanation.surface: Valiant warriors, already suffering, are beaten by a swordsman in a fatal battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the last E of the pain word, 'in' puts the fighters inside it, and 'overwhelmed by' wraps the swordsman round all of it. 'Blooming' is both a mild British curse and flowering.
explanation.definitionFit: A poisonous flowering plant of the potato family, so a bloom that can kill.

clue.text: Ancient Greeks born in ruins of Athens

indicators.note: the letter for born is placed within the rearranged city name
a city in ruins is wrecked, so its letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Some ancient Greeks were born amid the ruins of Athens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruins of' rearranges ATHENS to THEANS, and 'in' puts B inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Citizens of Thebes, a leading city of ancient Greece and rival to Athens.

clue.text: Loveliest porter working in London station

indicators.note: the words are put to work in a new order, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A charming porter is on duty at a London railway terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: A major railway terminus in the City of London, serving East Anglia.

clue.text: Pass two people adopting new name

indicators.note: the pair takes in the two letters, holding them inside

parts.note: a duo is a pair of people

explanation.surface: A couple adopting a child pass on choosing a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquial 'I don't know', what a quiz contestant says when declining to answer, which is to pass.

clue.text: Taking part in run invigorating? Not at first

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for invigorating is dropped

parts.note: bracing air is invigorating

explanation.surface: A jogger wonders whether taking part in a run is invigorating, at least not at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Competing in a race, such as a running event, is what someone doing this is up to.

clue.text: Watch tapes etc being unwound

indicators.note: tapes coming off their spools get jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Watch as tapes and other things are unwound.
explanation.definitionFit: To look on as an onlooker at an event, synonymous with observing.

clue.text: Very pleasant near European resort

indicators.note: the word for pleasant comes right next to the European letter

parts.note: nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: A very pleasant resort near somewhere European.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice is itself a resort, a red herring for the actual answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian lagoon city is a famous holiday destination for tourists.

clue.text: Heckle, wanting leader removed? That's the spirit

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for heckle must be taken away

parts.note: to barrack is to heckle or jeer

explanation.surface: A heckler is told to shut out the leader, and that's the spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's the spirit' sounds like encouragement, but spirit means a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcoholic liquor distilled in Asia from rice or palm sap, so a strong drink.

clue.text: First-class run towards pacific island, mostly going by plane

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written AI in crosswords
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: the island's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Borneo is an island in the western Pacific region

explanation.surface: A first-class trip to a peaceful island, mostly by air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pacific' is in lower case, so it reads as peaceful as well as naming the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Being carried through the air in flight, as passengers aboard an aircraft are.

clue.text: Crime is soon solved with involvement of Met's head: him?

definitions.text: Crime is soon solved with involvement of Met's head: him?

indicators.note: the initial letter is brought into the middle of the rearranged letters
a puzzle solved is worked out, so the letters are rearranged
the first letter of Met's is taken

explanation.surface: Crime is cleared up quickly once the head of the Metropolitan Police gets involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solved' turns CRIME IS SOON into COMISSIONER, and the M goes in. The Met is London's Metropolitan Police.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief of London's Metropolitan Police holds this title, so he is the Met's head.

clue.text: Interests son in English flowers

indicators.note: the son's letter is put inside the flowers

parts.note: roses are flowers

explanation.surface: A son takes an interest in English flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: To absorb someone's attention fully, a stronger synonym for holding their attention.

clue.text: Groups of islands forming curve in East African location

parts.note: an arc is a curve
in means fashionable, and so does hip
Lagos is the largest city in Nigeria

explanation.surface: Islands forming a curve in some East African spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' reads as a link but means trendy; Lagos is actually in West Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Clusters of islands in a sea, such as the Aegean groups, are known by this term.

clue.text: Maybe little friend's colourful collection?

parts.note: a pal is a friend
-ette is a suffix making things little, as in kitchenette

explanation.surface: A wonder whether some little friend owns a colourful collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' flags the pun: the answer could be read as a small pal.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's board holds a range of paints, and the word also means a range of colours.

clue.text: Pig eating fish and bird

indicators.note: the pig takes the fish inside it

parts.note: a sow is a female pig
a parr is a young salmon

explanation.surface: A pig eats some fish and a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A small brown songbird common in gardens and towns.

clue.text: Mother hen heard somewhere in Asia

parts.note: ma is mother

indicators.note: the word for a hen is taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a laying hen is a layer

explanation.surface: A mother hen is heard somewhere in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the R of layer is silent, so it sounds like LAYA.
explanation.definitionFit: The former name of the peninsula and federation now part of Malaysia, so a region of the continent.

clue.text: Show Liberal party is in front

indicators.note: the party word comes ahead of the letter for Liberal

parts.note: to carouse is to party

explanation.surface: A political observation that the Liberal party is ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rodgers and Hammerstein musical has this title, so it is a stage musical.

clue.text: Margaret initially affected by love letter

indicators.note: the love letter is placed beside the rest

parts.note: O, love, is zero in tennis
Meg is a short form of Margaret

indicators.note: the first letter of affected is taken

explanation.surface: Margaret is first moved by a love letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love letter' looks like one idea, but love is O and letter is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The last character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Tough amphibious creature biting old boy

indicators.note: the creature's word takes the old boy in its mouth, inside it

parts.note: a toad is an amphibian

explanation.surface: A tough toad bites an old schoolboy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tough' reads as an adjective for the creature, but it is the dismissive interjection.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dismissive interjections meaning hard luck, unfortunate but unchangeable.

clue.text: Servant wanting a dance

parts.note: a valet is a manservant

explanation.surface: A servant hopes for a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-time round ballroom dance in triple time.

clue.text: Leaders of the robbers, each certain to get riches

indicators.note: the first letters of the two words are taken

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: The heads of a robber gang are each sure of getting rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoarded wealth such as gold and jewels is a store of valuables.

clue.text: Board game played by fellow attending hospital department

parts.note: a man is a fellow

indicators.note: the word is played around with, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: ENT is ear, nose and throat

explanation.surface: A man plays a board game in a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board game' looks like one phrase; Board is the definition and 'played' rearranges GAME to AGEM.
explanation.definitionFit: A company's directors, the board, collectively run the firm.

clue.text: Cut waiting for a start in old hospital

indicators.note: the start letter goes inside the hospital

parts.note: san, short for sanatorium, is an old word for a hospital

indicators.note: the first letter of waiting is taken

explanation.surface: A patient waiting to start being cut in an old hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Past participle of the verb for sawing, so divided with a blade.
